learning_outcomes.text: Ability to solve mathematical problems that may arise in engineering. Aptitude to apply knowledge on: linear algebra.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity and critical reasoning.
Ability to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering, both orally and in writing, and to all types of audiences.
Honesty, responsibility, ethical commitment and spirit of solidarity.
Ability to work in a team.
Use the basic properties of real and complex numbers and perform fundamental operations with them.
Use the basic elements of Linear Algebra: systems of linear equations, vector spaces and linear applications and use matrices to simplify their study.
Identify metric properties in vector spaces, through scalar product, norm or distance.
Calculate eigenvalues and eigenvectors and diagonalize endomorphisms and matrices.
Solve geometric problems in the plane and in space.
Identify the basic elements of differential equations and systems of differential equations and use algebraic tools to solve elementary cases.

syllabus_topics: Topic 2. Systems of linear equations and matrices.
Solving systems using Gauss's Method. Application to inverse matrix calculation.
Linear combinations and linear independence. Bases and dimension. Coordinates.
Kernel and image of an application. Classification of linear applications.
Applications to solving systems of linear differential equations.
Euclidean vector space. Scalar product and metric properties.
Matrix calculation and systems of equations
Vector spaces and changes of basis

assessment_methods.method: Partial written control 1 (covers first three topics)
Partial written control 2 (covers last three topics)

assessment_rules: The final grade (NF) is calculated as: NF = 0.15*NL + maximum (0.15*NA + 0.7*NC, 0.85*NC). A minimum of 2.5 out of 10 points is required in each partial control. If this minimum is not reached in any control, the final grade will be a fail, and the numerical grade will be the minimum between NF and 4.5. Non-attendance to the ordinary call exam results in a 'NOT PRESENTED' grade. For differentiated evaluation, if classroom practice attendance is not possible, NF = 0.15*NL + 0.85*NC, with a pass if NF >= 5, NL >= 2.5, and NC >= 2.5 in each written part. Extraordinary calls involve a written exam (two parts) and a laboratory practice test, with the same grading formula.
